title: Personal LLM inference mini-tracker - Maya - Q3 2026
content:
Purpose: quick personal tracker for small experiments on batching, quantization, and KV-cache for latency/throughput tradeoffs. Mostly notes-to-self; copy results to team doc after cleaning.

Columns: date | model | quant | batch | seq_len | tokens/sec (avg) | p99 latency (ms) | cost / 1k tokens | notes / next steps

2026-07-12 | redwood-v1-7b | int8 | 1 | 64 | 420 | 120 | $0.28 | baseline single-request perf (no KV). Notice variance on headers; need stable prompt prefix. Next: run with prefix caching.
2026-07-13 | redwood-v1-7b | int8 | 4 | 64 | 1200 | 240 | $0.21 | batching helps throughput but p99 increases due to queueing. Try smaller max_batch_delay.
2026-07-14 | redwood-v1-7b | int8 | 8 | 64 | 2100 | 420 | $0.18 | good throughput, p99 unacceptable for sync UX. Evaluate async + callback.
2026-07-16 | redwood-v1-7b | int8 + kv-prefix | 1 | 64 | 900 | 95 | $0.19 | KV cache for repeated prefix gives big p99 wins. Clean up test harness to simulate realistic prefix cache hit rates.
2026-07-20 | redwood-v1-7b | int4 | 1 | 64 | 600 | 140 | $0.12 | quant int4 reduces cost but p99 slightly worse than int8; artifacts on some tokens. Tag for quality check.
2026-07-22 | redwood-v1-7b | int4 + kv | 4 | 128 | 2600 | 360 | $0.08 | high throughput at low cost but p99 still high for batched large seq. Consider dynamic batching policy by seq_len.
2026-07-28 | redwood-v1-13b | int8 | 1 | 256 | 230 | 240 | $0.72 | 13b has expected latency. For larger seq, consider model-slicing experiments (13b -> 7b fallback) for latency-sensitive requests.
2026-07-30 | redwood-v1-7b | int8 | 2 | 512 | 180 | 380 | $0.25 | large seq_len kills throughput; test KV segmentation (cache only prefix up to 128).

Quick observations / TODOs:
- KV cache is the biggest win for p99 on repeated prefixes. Need to add percentage-hit simulation (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) to estimate overall cost/latency impact.
- Batching: tune max_batch_delay and per-model min_batch to hit tail latency SLOs. Add a small script that increases delay until p99 crosses threshold.
- Quantization: int4 saves ~33-50% costs but sometimes introduces token artifacts for long seqs. Add eval prompts + BLEU/ROUGE-ish checks for degeneration.
- Multi-model routing: for <128 tokens route to 7b int8, for >=128 consider 13b on dedicated nodes or fallback to smaller models with progressive decoding. Need to simulate routing policy effect on overall infra cost.
- Add a column for cache_hit_rate in next iteration. Also track wall-clock runtime variability across warm/cold GPU state.

Scratch notes (unstructured):
- today: experiment harness uses synthetic prompts with varying prefix repetition; need to replace with sampled production prompts (ask SRE for sanitized sample)
- noticed spikes at ~30s into long-run. Might be GPU trimming or memory GC in runtime. File infra ticket? See ENG-1345.
- convo with Connor: try hybrid batching (persisted small batches for high-priority users). Prototype config in experiments/variant-A.

Next steps (short):
- 1) Add cache_hit_rate column and re-run July experiments sweeping 0-100% hit. (due 2026-08-07)
- 2) Create small evaluation set (~200 prompts) to detect quant artifacts. Run int4 vs int8 diffs. (due 2026-08-10)
- 3) Draft brief for team on dynamic batching heuristics + model-routing thresholds. Share for feedback.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc messy. When ready, copy results + sanitized tables into shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/experiment-summaries/ and open PR with graphs.
